What was once merely a carbide axe is now a florid work of art. Curling wires wind around the haft of the weapon as the creeping vine of a rose plant; modules and battery housing are mounted on the flat of its blade where the blossom might rest.

The air swims around the axe's triangular head like the heat off the high salt sun. Such a weapon of war seems a strange fit for an agrarian people like the hindren, but it serves to illustrate how cornered prey might react over long time scales.
Half battle axe and half vinereaper, the ancestral tool called Yal evokes the struggle between the hindren cultivators and the cruelty of a harsh winter. A biting cold radiates off the curved blade.
Beautiful ribbons of leaf are etched along the edges of the broad and oiled blade. The pine handle is carved with its name: Difucila.

Lifeblood the color of amaranth and dried in moonlight paints the clenched and giant fist of the dead forest Saad. The sight of it unfurls one of Time's right-blown ribbons: this is a relic in all or near-all futures, and the wielder perhaps =pronouns.possessive= fossil-mate and secret sharer.

Astragals demarcate the phasic slits along the frustum's length. Noise is sucked out of time in expectancy of cross-plane fusion.
